task.description:
Validate src/design/iss0629-tc-lua-10-03-flake-fix.md before BACKEND-DEV implements it. This is a small, test-only fix for GH-600: TC-LUA-10-03 in src/lua/limiter_wiring_test.zig intermittently fails due to a race between the watchdog thread's own 10ms poll interval and an immediate post-return assertion. Fix: replace the single assertion with a bounded (1000ms) yield-spin retry loop.

ORCH already independently verified: (1) POLL_INTERVAL_NS is genuinely 10ms in timeout.zig, (2) std.Thread.yield() is genuinely already used elsewhere in limiter_wiring_test.zig (line 623, the adjacent mutation-check test), (3) milliTimestamp() is genuinely a locally-defined helper already used throughout the file, (4) lint_design_artefact.py exits 0.

YOUR JOB: run your own full independent validation.
1. Read the design fresh.
2. Confirm the retry loop's placement and logic is correct -- verify it truly cannot mask a genuine watchdog failure (the loop only starts after the 1s deadline has already passed, since the 200M-iteration script takes far longer than 1s to run) -- trace through this reasoning yourself against the actual test file.
3. Confirm no production code (src/lua/timeout.zig) needs to change.
4. Confirm the scope-confirmation section's claim that TC-LUA-10-01, TC-LUA-10-02, and the TC-LUA-10-03 mutation-check test do NOT share this race pattern -- read those three tests yourself, don't just trust the design's characterization.
5. Confirm the yield-spin-over-sleep-based decision is well-justified (avoids needing to make timeout.zig's private sleepNanos public or re-deriving the same Windows/POSIX branch logic in test code).
acceptance_criteria: Retry loop placement/logic verified correct, cannot mask genuine failure
No production code changes confirmed necessary
Scope-confirmation claims verified against real other-test source

result.summary: Independently validated src/design/iss0629-tc-lua-10-03-flake-fix.md (GH-600). lint_design_artefact.py exits 0. Confirmed against live source: L600 of limiter_wiring_test.zig is exactly the single-shot assert the design targets; the proposed retry loop syntax mirrors an existing, already-compiling pattern at L621-624 (yield-spin) and reuses the already-declared local helper milliTimestamp() (L58, i64, used at L584/586/621/622) with no new imports. timeout.zig confirms POLL_INTERVAL_NS=10ms (L84) and watchdogLoop (L187-200) only sets fired after its own poll observes now>=deadline -- matching the design characterization exactly. Traced the no-masking argument directly: the retry loop only begins after lua_pcall returns, which is only after the 200M-iteration script (by test construction, L567-574) has already run longer than the 1s deadline, so the deadline is provably already past when the loop starts; if hasFired() is still false after a further full 1000ms, the final assert still fails exactly as before -- no failure mode is masked. Verified hasFired() is called nowhere else in the file except L600 (TC-LUA-10-03) and L632 (its mutation check on a never-started WatchdogState, which per WatchdogState.init defaults fired=false and has no thread to ever flip it) -- TC-LUA-10-01/mutation-check never call hasFired() at all, and TC-LUA-10-02/mutation-check read the watchdog only synchronously inline via platformCallService or bypass it entirely via executeMockedServiceCall, matching the design scope-confirmation claims exactly. Confirmed sleepNanos (timeout.zig L127) has no pub qualifier, so the yield-spin-over-reuse decision is correctly justified as avoiding a forbidden production-file change. No production code changes are proposed or needed -- confirmed timeout.zig is not touched anywhere in the design.
